title: Prefixes and two words
goal: Strike a prefix alone, then the word with the join key held; or join two whole words.

blocks.x: *over-* and *under-* are words themselves: [[overcome|AUFR/+KUPL]]. *dis-* and *mis-* are words too.

`ex-` and `dis-` have keys that join the next stroke's left hand, keeping the word one stroke: [[expect|KPEBGT]], [[distance|STKUPBS]]. `un-`, `mis-`, `over-`, `under-` and `inter-` fold the same way when their keys fit; when they clash with the stem's keys, the prefix is its own stroke, as above.
Both forms are in the dictionary, so which applies does not matter; the prefix stroke always works.

A compound is its two words, the second joined: [[myself|PHAOEU/+SEFL]], [[outside|OUT/+SAOEUD]]. Works for any compound you can split (*sun* + *light*), even where speech blurs the join: [[noone|PHO/+WUPB]] is *no* + *one*, [[cannot|K/+OT]] is *can* + *not*.

blocks.title: Prefix, then stem
blocks.x: Five joined words. Hold T or G with the second stroke.
